A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same COMMOD research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix D report original experiments on Law School and Compas, including fairness–accuracy tradeoffs, prediction changes, interpretability, and architecture comparisons.

after.justification: The original experiments are retained, and Section 6.4 adds a 20-seed sensitivity study with reported regression results.

M1.justification: The multiplicative logit update, linear concept architecture, adversarial objective, and ratio/concept penalties remain unchanged. The generalized distance formulation and expanded training documentation do not establish a revised procedure; both versions use the Euclidean ratio penalty in experiments.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate binary classification on Law School and Compas with race as the sensitive attribute, addressing demographic parity and equalized odds. The new sensitivity study repeats the existing experimental protocol without introducing additional dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain AdvDebias/Zhang, LPP, FRAPPE, Oracle (LPP), and Oracle (ROC). The interpretability and appendix comparisons also retain their comparator membership; new Table 1 summarizes the existing methods.

E3.justification: Section 6.4 adds a regression-based sensitivity protocol that repeats splitting and training, varies lambda_fair from 0.5 to 1.5 and lambda_ratio from 0.01 to 0.1, and conditions outcomes on initial-model performance and loss weights. The existing 70/30 split rule, logistic-regression base model, concept counts, and benchmark evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Section 6.4 investigates whether variation in COMMOD's three performance measures is explained by initial-model performance and hyperparameters. Existing Appendix D robustness, architecture, calibration, and post-hoc interpretability analyses remain. Removed Appendix B.2.1 contained symbolic count tables rather than experimental outcomes.

E5.justification: Beyond the retained five-run means and standard deviations in Figure 4, v2 introduces a separate 20-seed replication of the training pipeline with regression-based variation analysis. It also newly discloses that most earlier results used one seed. This substantially expands treatment of randomness, without converting all benchmark comparisons into repeated-run estimates.

E6.justification: New Table 1 reports numerical averages of prediction changes within demographic-parity fairness/accuracy quartiles. Section 6.4 adds R-squared values of 0.96, 0.99, and 0.97 for changes, accuracy, and fairness respectively. Existing plotted results and appendix numerical tables are retained; these additions do not demonstrate improved same-setting performance.

T1.justification: Equation 1 generalizes the similarity constraint to an expected discrepancy dist_phi. Definition 4.3 changes the switching point, and Proposition 4.4 adopts the strict condition K < Ks. Most substantially, v2 adds Proposition 4.5 and its Appendix B.2 proof concerning optimal flip allocation for equalized odds.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain controlled model debiasing, theoretical guarantees, and model-agnostic COMMOD achieving competitive fairness/accuracy with fewer, interpretable changes. The abstract now explicitly mentions binary classification, but this restriction was already stated in v1 Section 2.

C2.justification: Section 6.4 newly interprets the regression results as evidence that initial-model performance and hyperparameters dominate variation, with limited effects from other stochasticity. Section 6.2 also adds a rationale for discrete accuracy comparisons against label-flipping methods. Existing applicability qualifications and future-work limitations remain largely unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract adds a code-repository link, Section 5.3 explicitly identifies binary cross-entropy losses, and new Appendix C.1 supplies a training walkthrough and simplified pseudocode, including optional adversary warm-up. Existing hyperparameter grid limits are retained. These are documentation additions rather than demonstrated implementation changes.

R1.justification: V2 adds Khurana and Galhotra (2021) to the concept-learning discussion and references. It removes the introduction's assertion that previous debiasing interpretation was exclusively post-hoc, while retaining the main novelty claim and the existing related-work comparison.

P1.justification: V2 makes targeted rewrites to the motivation, formal setup, theory exposition, and evaluation explanations, and adds interpretability subheadings. It inserts Sections 6.4 and C.1 and removes the unfinished B.2.1 subsection, while preserving the overall narrative and section order.

P2.justification: V2 adds the demographic-parity summary Table 1 and an Algorithm 1 display, removes symbolic count tables, and reflows existing material with publication headers. All ten figures retain their plot content; existing appendix tables are principally renumbered and repositioned.

improvement.justification: The code link, training outline, numerical summary, and 20-seed analysis improve accessibility and empirical transparency. However, new Proposition 4.5 claims endpoint optimality for any K, while its Appendix B.2 proof assumes linear reductions without handling saturation or sign changes in the absolute rate gaps defined in Section 2.1.2. These useful additions coexist with a material new theoretical gap, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
